# Canonical acceptance specification for AI-02 (#31), M3.
# The owner-accepted manifest is docs/reports/omp-closeout/AI-02-MODEL-MANIFEST.md: Apache-2.0
# EmbeddingGemma 2 text 270M ONNX weights, onnxruntime CPU, this workstation only.
# SCN-3205 is @live-local: excluded from the default offline suite and executed under unshare -rn
# with the real local weights. The external Ollama endpoint does not satisfy this specification.
@AI-02 @issue-31 @M3
Feature: AI-02: Optional inference executes on the same machine
  Local inference is optional. Remote endpoints, implicit downloads, and remote execution do not
  satisfy it.

  Rule: Local inference is optional and remote execution is refused

    @SCN-3201
    Scenario: Default discovery needs no model runtime
      Given no local model runtime is installed
      And no local inference opt-in is configured
      When discovery is requested with no provider override
      Then discovery succeeds through "fake"
      And no model process is started
      And no model weights are downloaded
      And no network connection is attempted

    @SCN-3202
    Scenario: A remote endpoint cannot satisfy local inference mode
      Given local inference mode is configured with endpoint "http://192.0.2.10:11434"
      When that provider is requested for SCN-001
      Then the API returns a 400 problem with code "invalid-request"
      And no connection to that endpoint is attempted
      And no candidates are returned

    @SCN-3203
    Scenario Outline: Missing local weights or runtime produce an unavailable result
      Given local inference mode is explicitly enabled
      And <condition>
      When that provider is requested for SCN-001
      Then the API returns a 503 problem with code "retrieval-unavailable"
      And no automatic download or remote fallback occurs
      And accepted links, evidence, and findings are unchanged

      Examples:
        | condition                                                       |
        | its configured weights digest is absent from local storage      |
        | its installed weights do not match the configured digest        |
        | its weights are installed but the runtime package is unavailable |

  Rule: Contract behavior is independent of model quality

    @SCN-3204
    Scenario: The adapter passes the shared discovery contract offline
      Given the local provider adapter uses deterministic embedding and search transports
      When the shared CandidateDiscovery contract cases execute against it
      Then returned source IDs equal the requested source IDs
      And candidate counts obey top_k and relation filters
      And ranks are contiguous from one
      And every candidate carries provider, model_version, and index_revision
      And no candidate carries a link ID or review state
      And a known artifact with no eligible targets returns an empty list with retained provenance
      And a runtime that cannot report its model identity fails explicitly without candidates
      And accepted links, evidence, and findings are unchanged

    @SCN-3205 @live-local
    Scenario: Real indexing and discovery work with external egress denied
      Given the owner-accepted local model manifest identifies installed weights and runtime
      And non-loopback egress is denied for the inference process tree
      And an isolated banking-demo index has not yet been built
      When that runtime indexes baseline-a and executes the shared discovery contract cases
      Then the contract cases complete without external network access
      And the execution record names the weights digest and runtime version
      And it records the query and document formatting versions
      And the live record retains the egress-denial observation
      And the observed weights, runtime, and formatting match the identified manifest
      And every returned candidate identifies that model and its snapshot binding

    @SCN-3206
    Scenario: Malformed local inference output is not an empty success
      Given the local adapter receives a non-finite embedding through its deterministic transport
      When discovery is requested for SCN-001
      Then a typed retrieval-unavailable problem is returned
      And no partial candidate list is returned
      And no accepted link, evidence, or finding is written

# Canonical acceptance specification for AI-03 (#32), M3.
# The retrieval snapshot/cache re-scope is owner-accepted in ADR 0012 §2. CTA owns content-hash
# planning, cache keys, manifests, isolated publication, compatibility, and honest refresh
# reporting. CocoIndex owns chunking/embeddings/index storage; CTA reports unobservable backend
# embedding counts as `not_available` and never infers them. Normative notes: docs/stories/AI-03.md.
@AI-03 @issue-32 @M3
Feature: AI-03: Revision-aware retrieval snapshot and cache lifecycle
  CTA owns content-change planning, manifests, isolated snapshot publication, compatibility, and
  candidate provenance. CocoIndex owns code chunking, embeddings, and its internal index.

  Rule: Refresh planning uses artifact content and explicit configuration

    @SCN-3301
    Scenario: Plan the banking fixture content changes
      Given a retrieval manifest for banking-demo baseline-a
      And the eligible corpus contains source and test artifacts
      When the refresh planner compares baseline-a with baseline-b
      Then changed artifacts are exactly CODE-001 and TEST-002
      And unchanged artifacts are exactly CODE-002 and TEST-001
      And the plan records both resolved revisions
      And the current and referenced previous manifests record their respective artifact content hashes
      And the plan does not claim that CocoIndex embedded exactly two items

    @SCN-3302
    Scenario: An evidence-only commit permits content reuse
      Given two commits have identical eligible artifact IDs, paths, and content hashes
      And their model and retrieval configuration are identical
      When refresh manifests are built for both commits
      Then both manifests have the same corpus cache key
      And their snapshot bindings identify their respective commits
      And the content-change plan is empty
      And no source change or verification failure is inferred from the different commits

    @SCN-3303
    Scenario: A model change invalidates compatibility
      Given an existing manifest and unchanged artifact content
      When a manifest is requested with a different weights digest
      Then the corpus cache key differs
      And the old cache is not declared compatible with the new model
      And the old manifest remains unchanged

  Rule: Snapshot publication and result combination preserve one provenance context

    @SCN-3304
    Scenario: Failed refresh leaves the previous snapshot usable
      Given baseline-a has a published retrieval manifest
      And the deterministic index adapter fails while building baseline-b
      When refresh is requested for baseline-b
      Then refresh reports a typed failure
      And no baseline-b snapshot is published
      And requests explicitly naming baseline-a still use its original manifest
      And requests naming baseline-b do not receive baseline-a results as a substitute

    @SCN-3305
    Scenario: Mixed snapshot candidates cannot form one ranked list
      Given one candidate batch is bound to baseline-a's manifest snapshot binding
      And the batch retains the provider's own index revision
      And another candidate batch is bound to baseline-b's manifest snapshot binding
      When the batches are submitted to the candidate-combination service
      Then combination fails with code "mixed-index-context"
      And no combined ranked list is returned
      When the baseline-a batch is submitted with the expected binding
      Then a ranked list is returned
      And every candidate carries the CTA snapshot binding
      And the batch provenance retains the provider's own index revision

    @SCN-3306
    Scenario: Refresh cost distinguishes measurements from unavailable backend data
      Given the deterministic search transport exposes no embedding counter
      When a baseline-b refresh completes
      Then its report contains measured non-negative elapsed time
      And it contains added, changed, removed, and unchanged artifact counts
      And items_embedded is null with availability "not_available"
      And the report identifies the published snapshot binding and configuration digest

  Retrieval quality is measured against hand-labeled fixture candidates, never treated as

    @SCN-2601

    @SCN-2602

      When the labeled dataset changes
      Then the previous report remains with its recorded dataset hash
      And a new report names the new hash

    @SCN-2603

      Given no network, model, or vector service
      When the evaluation harness runs

# Canonical acceptance specification for AI-06 (#56), M3.
# Source criteria: the RAG mission's PR 1 slice ("CocoIndex Code compatibility, integration
# contract, and live smoke") and the adoption decision recorded in docs/adr/0008.
# This is an implementation-approach story under F-08. It does not amend or close AI-01 (#30),
# AI-02 (#31), AI-03 (#32), AI-04 (#34), or AI-05 (#35). CocoIndex Code supplies semantic
# code-search observations; CTA keeps artifact identity, accepted links, evidence, and policy.
# These scenarios are mapped to pytest checks; no Gherkin runner executes them.
@AI-06 @issue-56 @M3
Feature: AI-06: CocoIndex Code semantic code-search capability and integration contract
  As a developer, I want an optional, bounded CocoIndex Code adapter that returns attributable
  source-code hits from one configured project snapshot, so that semantic code retrieval can be
  integrated later without weakening CTA's offline default or its separation of proposals,
  accepted relationships, and verification evidence.

  Rule: CocoIndex is optional and never required by default paths.

    @SCN-1001
    Scenario: Offline default is unchanged
      Given no CocoIndex executable, project root, daemon, or embedding endpoint is configured
      When the default configuration is loaded and a discovery request runs
      Then discovery uses the deterministic "fake" provider
      And no CocoIndex process is started
      And no CocoIndex index is accessed and no network request is made
      And "cocoindex" is not a registered discovery provider in this slice

  Rule: Requests and results are bounded observations.

    @SCN-1002
    Scenario: Search requests are bounded before execution
      Given a CocoIndex client with configured request bounds
      When a search requests a limit of 1 or 100, a non-negative offset, and a non-empty query
      Then the request is accepted
      And a limit of 0 or 101, a negative offset, an empty or over-2000-character query, or more than 10 path or language filters is rejected with "cocoindex-request-error" before any process starts
      And a path filter that is absolute, carries a drive or UNC prefix, contains a parent-directory component, or does not use relative POSIX path syntax is rejected with "cocoindex-request-error"
      And response bytes, per-hit content, and captured stderr have configurable limits

    @SCN-1003
    Scenario: A structured search returns normalized hits
      Given a captured structured result and a configured project root
      When the client normalizes the result
      Then it preserves the reported order and any duplicate chunks
      And every hit reports its project-relative path, language, 1-based line range, content, and score as reported
      And the configured project root is recorded as caller-supplied context, not as observed index identity
      And the server name and version are recorded when the server reports them
      And the index identity is reported as unavailable because the MCP contract does not expose it
      And a valid empty result is a success with no hits
      And no hit exposes a link id, review state, evidence id, verification claim, or assurance conclusion

    @SCN-1004
    Scenario: Malformed results are rejected whole, never repaired
      Given a result with an absolute path, a parent-directory escape, an empty path, an invalid line range, a non-finite score, a wrong field type, missing or non-text content, a mismatched response id, an MCP error flag, inconsistent counts, or a response beyond the configured bound
      When the client normalizes the result
      Then it raises "cocoindex-protocol-error"
      And the entire response is rejected, including any otherwise-valid hits, instead of returning a partial list
      And no invalid hit is dropped, clamped, or rewritten
      And no artifact identity is invented

    @SCN-1005
    Scenario Outline: Failures are typed and owned processes are reaped
      Given <condition>
      When a search is attempted
      Then it raises "<error>"
      And a process the adapter started is terminated and reaped within the configured cleanup interval, without stopping an unrelated shared daemon
      And the caller receives no hit list

      Examples:
        | condition                                            | error                         |
        | the executable is missing                            | cocoindex-configuration-error |
        | the project root has no CocoIndex settings marker    | cocoindex-configuration-error |
        | the server name, version, or search schema is incompatible | cocoindex-capability-error |
        | the server exits before initialize                   | cocoindex-unavailable         |
        | the server closes its output pipe                    | cocoindex-unavailable         |
        | the server exits non-zero                            | cocoindex-unavailable         |
        | the server does not answer before the deadline       | cocoindex-timeout             |
        | the server ignores termination after the deadline    | cocoindex-timeout             |
        | the search reports success false, even with partial results | cocoindex-query-error   |

  Rule: The adapter selects one configured project and validates what it returns.

    @SCN-1006
    Scenario: Only the configured project is selected and returned paths are validated
      Given a configured project root containing CocoIndex settings
      When the client searches
      Then the server runs with that project root as its working directory
      And the adapter refuses to use the default shared CocoIndex state directory
      And the adapter never falls back to an ancestor CocoIndex project
      And only allow-listed subprocess environment variables are passed
      And when hits are verified against the snapshot, a missing file, a symlink resolving outside the root, a line range beyond end of file, or content that differs from the declared comparison rule is rejected

  Rule: Indexed repository text is untrusted data, not instruction.

    @SCN-1007
    Scenario: Instruction-like text stays data
      Given an indexed source file whose comments contain instruction-like text
      When the search returns a hit for that file
      Then the text is carried as data in the hit
      And it creates no link, review decision, evidence record, policy change, verification claim, or coverage claim

  Rule: Live integration evidence is explicit, attributable, and optional.

    @SCN-1008
    Scenario: Without live opt-in the probe reports NOT RUN
      Given live opt-in is not enabled

  CocoIndex Code finds code and test chunks. CTA maps them to authoritative artifacts at one
  commit. A hit is a proposal: it is never an accepted link, review state, or verification evidence.

  Rule: Every candidate is bound to one immutable snapshot

    @SCN-2301
    Scenario: CocoIndex hits map to canonical baseline-bound artifacts
      Given the fixture repository ingested at "baseline-a"
      When code discovery runs for "SCN-001" with the captured CocoIndex response
      Then the candidates are canonical source artifacts "CODE-002" and "CODE-001"
      And each candidate carries path, line range, revision, content hash, method, and snapshot binding
      And the unannotated path "src/__init__.py" is reported unresolved
      And accepted and proposed links and verification evidence are unchanged

    @SCN-2302
    Scenario: The same query at baseline-b is bound to baseline-b
      Given the fixture repository ingested at "baseline-b"
      When code discovery runs for "SCN-001" with the captured CocoIndex response
      Then every candidate revision is the baseline-b commit
      And the snapshot binding and the changed artifact hash differ from baseline-a

    @SCN-2303
    Scenario: A configured project at another commit is rejected
      Given a live-mode CocoIndex discovery over the fixture repository
      When code discovery requests "baseline-a" while the project is checked out at baseline-b
      Then retrieval fails with an explicit cross-baseline error
      And no candidate from the wrong snapshot is returned

  Rule: Missing capability is not an empty success

    @SCN-2304
    Scenario: Unconfigured CocoIndex reports not available
      Given the fixture repository ingested at "baseline-a"
      When code discovery explicitly requests CocoIndex without configuration
      Then the response status is "not_available"
      And no candidate or fabricated index identity is returned

  Rule: A deterministic lexical baseline uses the same snapshot

    @SCN-2305
    Scenario: Lexical retrieval is deterministic
      Given the fixture repository ingested at "baseline-a"
      When lexical code discovery runs twice for "SCN-001"
      Then both runs return the same candidates, scores, and snapshot binding
      And "CODE-001" is the first candidate

  Rule: Discovery never mutates the engineering graph

    @SCN-2306
    Scenario: Discovery writes no relationships or evidence
      Given the fixture repository ingested at "baseline-a"
      When code discovery runs for "SCN-001"
      Then the accepted links, proposed links, artifacts, and evidence equal their prior values
      And no finding is produced by retrieval

    @SCN-2307
    Scenario: A requirement is not code-discovered as if it were a scenario
      Given the fixture repository ingested at "baseline-a"
      When code discovery requests the requirement "REQ-001"
      Then retrieval is rejected because code discovery requires a scenario
      And no requirement-to-code relationship is created

  Rule: Retrieved text is untrusted data

    @SCN-2308
    Scenario: Instruction-like hit text cannot change policy
      Given a captured CocoIndex response whose hit content says to accept a link
      When code discovery runs for "SCN-001" with that response
      Then the hit is reported unresolved because its bytes do not match the commit
      And no accepted link, review state, evidence, or assurance finding changes

@AS-03 @issue-4 @M2
Feature: AS-03: Keep failed, missing, and potentially stale evidence distinct
  One evaluation can contain all three situations. Their meanings are different and their
  precedence is declared: a confirmed failure at the evaluated baseline wins for its scenario;
  a stale pass is a request for reverification; a missing accepted link is a coverage gap.

    Scenario: Distinguish missing, failed, and stale evidence in one evaluation
      Given "REQ-001" has passing verification evidence at baseline "baseline-a"
      And "REQ-002" has no accepted verification scenario
      And "REQ-003" has a failing test at baseline "baseline-b"
      And a relevant linked implementation of "REQ-001" changed at baseline "baseline-b"
      When assurance evaluates baseline "baseline-b"
      Then "REQ-002" yields a "missing_verification_link" finding
      And "REQ-003" yields a "verification_failed" finding
      And "REQ-001" yields a "reverification_required" finding
      And no finding downgrades "reverification_required" to "verification_failed"

  Rule: Applicability is decided by content, not commit identity

    @SCN-2032
    Scenario: Evidence recorded at a source commit applies to its evidence commit
      Given evidence "EV-001" was recorded at the source commit of "baseline-a"
      And the evidence commit stores the report without changing artifact content
      When assurance evaluates baseline "baseline-a"
      Then the evidence is treated as applicable
      And "REQ-001" has no "verification_failed" finding

# docs/adr/0012-closeout-scope-decisions.md §1 (trusted-local-operator identity, append-only

# Contract notes (baseline selection, snapshot identity, journal events, workspace response shapes)
# are normative in docs/stories/AS-06.md and docs/domain-contracts.md.
@AS-06 @issue-28 @M3
Feature: AS-06: Human decisions on version-bound proposals
  Discovery proposals become accepted relationships only through an explicit capture action and a
  human decision. Decisions are durable audit events, and acceptance never changes evidence or
  assurance findings. A review decision names the baseline it was evaluated against explicitly;
  an omitted baseline is a request-validation error, never a silent "latest" choice.

  Background:
    Given banking-demo baseline-a is loaded
    And the review journal is empty and outside the fixture repository
    And trusted-local-operator mode identifies the operator as "rv-ana"

  Rule: Discovery candidates become reviewable proposals only through explicit capture

    @SCN-3001
    Scenario: Capture a candidate without accepting it
      Given fake discovery returned SCN-002 implemented_by CODE-001
      When the operator submits that candidate and its baseline-a endpoint hashes to POST "/api/link-proposals"
      Then a new link is returned with review_state "proposed"
      And its snapshot retains the submitted provider, model version, and index revision
      And its snapshot identifies baseline-a and both endpoint content hashes
      And its snapshot digest is the canonical hash of the snapshot identity fields
      And no accepted link, verification evidence, or assurance finding is created
      And every file in the fixture repository retains its original content hash

    @SCN-3012
    Scenario Outline: Refuse an invalid capture without publishing a proposal
      Given the review journal is empty
      When the operator submits a capture with "<defect>"
      Then the response is a <status> problem with code "<code>"
      And no proposal or decision is appended

      Examples:
        | defect                             | status | code             |
        | an unknown target artifact SCN-999 | 422    | proposal-invalid |
        | a relation direction that contradicts the endpoint artifact types | 422 | proposal-invalid |
        | a source content hash that disagrees | 409 | proposal-stale |
        | a target content hash that disagrees | 409 | proposal-stale |

    @SCN-3013
    Scenario: Repeating an identical capture returns the existing proposal
      Given a captured proposal for SCN-002 implemented_by CODE-001 at baseline-a
      When the operator submits the identical snapshot again
      Then the response is 200 with the existing link and snapshot
      And the journal still contains exactly one capture event for that proposal

    @SCN-3021
    Scenario Outline: Capture conflicts are typed and publish nothing
      Given a captured proposal for SCN-002 implemented_by CODE-001 at baseline-a
      When the operator submits "<submission>"
      Then the response is a 409 problem with code "<code>"
      And the journal still contains exactly one capture event for that proposal

      Examples:
        | submission                                            | code              |
        | the same endpoints with a different provider identity | proposal-conflict |
        | the same endpoints after a terminal decision          | review-conflict   |

    @SCN-3018
    Scenario: An evidence-only revision change remains reviewable
      Given a captured proposal for SCN-002 implemented_by CODE-001 at baseline-a
      And an evidence-only revision exists whose endpoint content hashes equal baseline-a
      When the operator accepts that proposal against that evidence-only revision
      Then the response contains the proposal with review_state "accepted"
      And the decision identifies the selected commit and the unchanged endpoint hashes
      And no source change or verification failure is inferred from the different commit

    @SCN-3029
    Scenario Outline: Capture persistence failure is bounded
      Given a valid capture for SCN-002 implemented_by CODE-001 at baseline-a
      And the journal <failure>
      When the operator submits that capture
      Then the response is a 503 problem with code "review-storage-unavailable"
      And its durability is "<durability>"
      And the live workspace <live>
      And restarting <restart>

      Examples:
        | failure                                                                 | durability    | live                                            | restart                                    |
        | fails and rolls back to its prior committed length                      | not_committed | does not list the proposal or an accepted link   | exposes no captured proposal               |
        | writes a complete pair but cannot confirm durability or roll it back    | indeterminate | does not list the proposal optimistically       | exposes either no proposal or one complete pending captured proposal, never an accepted link |

  Rule: Decisions are durable audit events and do not perform verification

    @SCN-3002
    Scenario: Accept the existing pending proposal
      Given LNK-007 is proposed at baseline-a
      And baseline findings and evidence have been recorded for comparison
      When "rv-ana" posts decision "accept" for LNK-007 at baseline-a
      Then the response contains LNK-007 with review_state "accepted"
      And the journal contains one decision identifying "rv-ana" and a server UTC timestamp
      And that decision identifies the proposal snapshot and baseline-a endpoint hashes
      And the workspace thread contains LNK-007 only in accepted_links
      And the workspace pending queue excludes LNK-007
      And workspace history returns that acceptance
      And baseline findings and evidence equal the recorded values
      And default baseline thread reads equal their values before the decision

    @SCN-3003
    Scenario: Reject a proposal with a retained reason
      Given LNK-007 is proposed at baseline-a
      When "rv-ana" rejects LNK-007 at baseline-a with reason "The scenario does not cover the requirement"
      Then the journal contains one rejection with that reason
      And the workspace history returns that rejection
      And LNK-007 is absent from the workspace accepted links and pending queue
      And LNK-007 is labelled as rejected for that baseline
      And baseline findings, evidence, and fixture file hashes are unchanged

    @SCN-3004
    Scenario: Refuse a decision supplied under another reviewer identity
      Given LNK-007 is proposed at baseline-a
      When "rv-mallory" posts decision "accept" for LNK-007 at baseline-a
      Then the response is a 403 problem with code "review-identity-mismatch"
      And no decision is appended
      And the workspace still shows LNK-007 as proposed

    @SCN-3005
    Scenario Outline: Refuse a rejection whose reason field is absent or null
      Given LNK-007 is proposed at baseline-a
      When "rv-ana" rejects LNK-007 at baseline-a with <input>
      Then the response is a 422 problem with code "request-validation"
      And no decision is appended

      Examples:
        | input           |
        | no reason field |
        | a null reason   |

    @SCN-3006
    Scenario Outline: Refuse a rejection whose reason is blank
      Given LNK-007 is proposed at baseline-a
      When "rv-ana" rejects LNK-007 at baseline-a with <input>
      Then the response is a 422 problem with code "review-reason-required"
      And no decision is appended

      Examples:
        | input                              |
        | an empty reason                    |
        | a reason of three space characters |

    @SCN-3007
    Scenario: Refuse review when no operator identity is configured
      Given the application has no configured operator identity
      When "rv-ana" posts decision "accept" for LNK-007 at baseline-a
      Then the response is a 503 problem with code "review-identity-unavailable"
      And no decision is appended

    @SCN-3008
    Scenario: Refuse a second terminal decision
      Given a durable acceptance decision already exists for LNK-007 at baseline-a
      When "rv-ana" posts decision "reject" for LNK-007 at baseline-a with reason "Changed my mind"
      Then the response is a 409 problem with code "review-conflict"
      And the original decision bytes are unchanged
      And no second decision is appended

    @SCN-3009
    Scenario: Refuse acceptance against changed endpoint content
      Given a captured proposal connects SCN-002 to CODE-001 at baseline-a
      And CODE-001 has different content at baseline-b
      When the operator accepts that proposal against baseline-b
      Then the response is a 409 problem with code "proposal-stale"
      And no decision is appended
      And no verification failure is recorded

    @SCN-3010
    Scenario: Failed persistence with a successful rollback does not publish an acceptance
      Given LNK-007 is proposed at baseline-a
      And the journal cannot durably append a record and can roll back to its prior committed length
      When "rv-ana" posts decision "accept" for LNK-007 at baseline-a
      Then the response is a 503 problem with code "review-storage-unavailable"
      And its durability is "not_committed"
      And the workspace still shows LNK-007 as proposed
      And restarting with the same journal does not expose an accepted decision

    @SCN-3028
    Scenario: An unconfirmed commit is reported as indeterminate
      Given LNK-007 is proposed at baseline-a
      And the journal writes a complete commit pair but cannot confirm its durability or roll it back
      When "rv-ana" posts decision "accept" for LNK-007 at baseline-a
      Then the response is a 503 problem with code "review-storage-unavailable"
      And its durability is "indeterminate"
      And the application does not report the decision as successful
      And further journal mutations are refused with "review-storage-unavailable"
      And restarting exposes either no decision or exactly one complete committed decision
      And no partial or malformed record is replayed

    @SCN-3011
    Scenario: Refuse a missing proposal
      When "rv-ana" posts decision "accept" for LNK-999 at baseline-a
      Then the response is a 404 problem with code "proposal-not-found"
      And no decision is appended

    @SCN-3014
    Scenario: Captures and decisions survive restart
      Given a captured proposal for SCN-002 implemented_by CODE-001 at baseline-a
      And "rv-ana" accepts that proposal at baseline-a
      When the application restarts with the same journal
      Then the workspace thread contains that proposal only in accepted_links
      And the workspace pending queue excludes that proposal
      And the workspace pending queue still lists the unrelated pending proposal LNK-007
      And the workspace history returns the capture and the acceptance
      And the decision identifies the same snapshot and operator
      And the journal bytes are identical to their bytes before restart

    @SCN-3023
    Scenario: A pending capture survives restart without a decision
      Given a captured proposal for SCN-002 implemented_by CODE-001 at baseline-a
      When the application restarts with the same journal
      Then the workspace pending queue lists that proposal with its snapshot and provenance
      And the workspace history returns its capture event
      And no accepted link or decision exists for it
      And the journal bytes are identical to their bytes before restart

    @SCN-3024
    Scenario: A rejection survives restart with its reason
      Given a captured proposal for SCN-002 implemented_by CODE-001 at baseline-a
      And "rv-ana" rejects that proposal at baseline-a with reason "The candidate is not the implementation"
      When the application restarts with the same journal
      Then the workspace history returns the rejection with its reason and operator
      And the proposal is absent from accepted links and the pending queue
      And the journal bytes are identical to their bytes before restart

    @SCN-3015
    Scenario: A later decision preserves earlier decision bytes
      Given a captured proposal for SCN-002 implemented_by CODE-001 at baseline-a
      And a captured proposal for SCN-002 exercised_by TEST-002 at baseline-a
      And the first proposal is rejected with reason "Not the right implementation"
      When "rv-ana" accepts the second proposal at baseline-a
      Then the first decision's journal bytes are unchanged
      And the workspace history returns both decisions
      And the first proposal remains absent from accepted links and pending

    @SCN-3016
    Scenario: Concurrent terminal decisions serialize
      Given LNK-007 is proposed at baseline-a
      When "rv-ana" submits an acceptance and a rejection for LNK-007 at baseline-a concurrently
      Then exactly one request returns a successful decision
      And the other request returns a 409 problem with code "review-conflict"
      And exactly one terminal decision event is appended
      And the workspace thread and pending queue agree with that decision

    @SCN-3017
    Scenario Outline: Refuse a review write outside the trusted local boundary
      Given LNK-007 is proposed at baseline-a
      When a decision request arrives with <condition>
      Then the response is a <status> problem with code "<code>"
      And no decision is appended

      Examples:
        | condition                                   | status | code                     |
        | a non-loopback client address               | 403    | review-loopback-required |
        | a browser Origin of https://example.invalid | 403    | review-origin-forbidden  |

    @SCN-3022
    Scenario: A loopback request without a browser Origin is allowed
      Given LNK-007 is proposed at baseline-a
      When "rv-ana" posts decision "accept" for LNK-007 at baseline-a without an Origin header
      Then the response is 200 with LNK-007 accepted
      And the journal contains one decision

    @SCN-3019
    Scenario: Decisions apply only under compatible endpoint content
      Given a captured proposal for SCN-002 implemented_by CODE-001 at baseline-a
      And the proposal is accepted at baseline-a
      When the workspace is read at baseline-a and at baseline-b
      Then baseline-a shows the proposal as accepted
      And baseline-b shows the same acceptance only if both endpoint hashes are unchanged
      And neither workspace shows an acceptance whose endpoint content differs from the snapshot
      And default baseline reads remain unchanged

    @SCN-3020 @browser
    Scenario: Review workspace shows provenance, decisions, and history
      Given banking-demo baseline-a is loaded
      And trusted-local-operator mode identifies the operator as "rv-ana"
      And the review journal is empty
      When the reviewer captures the fake candidate for SCN-002 implemented_by CODE-001 at baseline-a
      And the reviewer opens the review workspace for REQ-002
      Then the proposal shows provider "fake", model version "fake-fixture-v1", and its index revision
      And the proposal is labelled as fixture-generated
      And the review controls require a reason for rejection
      When the reviewer accepts the proposal
      Then the workspace shows the proposal as accepted and excludes it from the pending queue
      And the history shows one acceptance by "rv-ana" with a server timestamp

    @SCN-3025 @browser
    Scenario: Rejection is visible with its retained reason and history
      Given banking-demo baseline-a is loaded
      And trusted-local-operator mode identifies the operator as "rv-ana"
      And the review journal is empty
      When the reviewer captures the fake candidate for SCN-002 implemented_by CODE-001 at baseline-a
      And the reviewer opens the review workspace for REQ-002
      And the reviewer rejects the proposal with reason "Not the right implementation"
      Then the workspace excludes the proposal from accepted links and the pending queue
      And the history shows one rejection by "rv-ana" with that reason and a server timestamp
      And the proposal remains absent from default baseline accepted links

    @SCN-3026 @browser
    Scenario: A refused review write is reported without a success state
      Given banking-demo baseline-a is loaded
      And trusted-local-operator mode identifies the operator as "rv-ana"
      And the review journal is empty
      When the reviewer captures the fake candidate for SCN-002 implemented_by CODE-001 at baseline-a
      And the reviewer opens the review workspace for REQ-002 and displays the pending acceptance control
      And the proposal is accepted through the API in another local request
      And the reviewer submits the already displayed acceptance control without refreshing
      Then the dashboard displays the typed review conflict
      And it does not display the proposal as newly accepted
      And refreshing the workspace shows the proposal as accepted by the earlier decision
      And the journal contains exactly one terminal decision

    @SCN-3027
    Scenario: An uncommitted journal tail blocks further mutations
      Given a captured proposal for SCN-002 implemented_by CODE-001 at baseline-a
      And the journal ends with a complete payload record lacking a commit marker
      When the application restarts with the same journal
      Then the uncommitted record is not replayed
      And a new review mutation is refused with a 503 problem and code "review-storage-unavailable"
      And no new journal record is appended

# Canonical acceptance specification for AS-07 (#29), M3.
# Derived from the owner's issue and the Codex advisory. Provider failure remains distinct from
# findings, empty success, and accepted coverage. Provenance presentation and problem-extension
# contracts are normative in docs/stories/AS-07.md and docs/domain-contracts.md.
@AS-07 @issue-29 @M3
Feature: AS-07: Honest provider availability and proposal provenance
  Provider failure remains distinct from findings, empty success, and accepted coverage. The
  dashboard never substitutes one provider's output for another's, and every proposal
  presentation identifies the provider, model version, and index identity it actually has.

  Rule: Provider failure remains distinct from findings and empty success

    @SCN-3101 @browser
    Scenario: An unregistered provider fails while baseline data remains usable
      Given the effective discovery registry contains only "fake"
      And the dashboard displays REQ-001 at baseline-a
      When discovery is requested with provider "missing-provider"
      Then the API returns a 400 problem with code "provider-not-registered"
      And failed_provider is "missing-provider"
      And registered_providers is ["fake"]
      And the candidate panel displays the selected provider as unavailable and names "missing-provider"
      And the candidate panel lists the registered providers and keeps "fake" selectable
      And the accepted thread and EV-001 remain accessible
      And no assurance finding is created

    @SCN-3102 @browser
    Scenario: A registered provider fails after an earlier successful request
      Given the configured provider "cocoindex" previously returned candidates for baseline-a
      And that provider now times out through its deterministic recorded transport
      When discovery is requested for baseline-b
      Then the API returns a 503 problem with code "provider-unavailable"
      And failed_provider is "cocoindex"
      And the panel displays the provider failure and names "cocoindex"
      And no baseline-a candidate appears as a current baseline-b result
      And no successful empty-result state is displayed
      And the application does not silently request fake discovery
      And the accepted thread and EV-001 remain accessible
      And accepted links, evidence, and findings are unchanged

    @SCN-3103 @browser
    Scenario: A valid empty result is not an unavailable provider
      Given the configured discovery provider is "fake"
      When candidates are requested for REQ-003 at baseline-a
      Then the API returns 200 with an empty candidates array
      And the response retains provider, model_version, and index_revision
      And the panel displays zero candidates without an unavailable-provider state

  Rule: Proposal provenance and acceptance state are visible separately

    @SCN-3104 @browser
    Scenario: A fixture proposal retains its provenance through review
      Given LNK-007 is displayed in the proposal panel at baseline-a
      And a rejection decision for LNK-007 is recorded with reason "Not this scenario"
      When its details and review history are opened
      Then every proposal presentation displays provider "fake"
      And every proposal presentation displays model_version "fake-fixture-v1"
      And every proposal presentation displays its recorded index_revision
      And it is labelled as fixture-generated
      And the review history retains that provenance with the rejection
      And it is absent from accepted_links

    @SCN-3105 @browser
    Scenario: A model-backed adapter is distinguishable without a live model test
      Given the CocoIndex provider adapter uses a deterministic recorded search transport
      And the real discovery route and problem mapping are exercised
      When its mapped proposal is displayed
      Then the panel identifies the provider as "cocoindex"
      And it displays the recorded model identity
      And it labels the snapshot value as a CTA snapshot binding
      And it does not label the proposal as fixture-generated or accepted
      And this check establishes adapter/API/UI behaviour, not live inference or retrieval quality

    @SCN-3106 @browser
    Scenario Outline: Historical missing provenance is shown as unknown
      Given a historical proposed link whose <field> is <value>
      When the proposal is displayed
      Then <field> is shown as "not recorded"
      And no current <field> is substituted
      And the proposal remains outside accepted_links

      Examples:
        | field          | value  |
        | provider       | absent |
        | provider       | null   |
        | model_version  | absent |
        | model_version  | null   |
        | index_revision | absent |
        | index_revision | null   |

    @SCN-3107 @browser
    Scenario: A historical model-backed proposal remains labelled when its provider is disabled
      Given a recorded proposal whose provider is "cocoindex" and whose model and index identity are recorded
      And the effective discovery registry contains only "fake"
      When the proposal is displayed in history
      Then the panel identifies the provider as "cocoindex"
      And it displays the recorded model identity
      And it labels the recorded index value as a CTA snapshot binding
      And it does not label the proposal as fixture-generated
      And it reports the provider as currently unavailable without hiding the recorded provenance

Feature: CI-01: Assurance evaluates and reports the triggering revision
  Evaluation is pinned, reproducible, offline, and independent of inference. Tool failure is not a
  finding.

  Rule: Evaluation is pinned, reproducible, and independent of inference

    @SCN-3401
    Scenario: Evaluate a pinned repository revision offline
      Given banking-demo baseline-b resolves to its fixture commit
      And dependencies are provisioned and external network access is denied
      And no model provider is enabled
      When the assurance command ingests and evaluates that commit
      Then it exits 0
      And its complete report identifies banking-demo and the resolved baseline-b commit
      And the report records the CTA evaluator revision and input content hashes
      And its findings match the hand-labeled baseline-b oracle
      And its report is stored outside the evaluated repository

    @SCN-3402
    Scenario: A PR event selects its head revision
      Given a deterministic PR event contains different head and test-merge SHAs
      When the workflow revision resolver processes that event
      Then the selected evaluated revision equals the event head SHA
      And the report records that exact selected revision
      And no test-merge SHA is reported as the head revision

    @SCN-3403
    Scenario: Self-ingestion reports supported assurance scope
      Given a pinned CTA checkout and an attributable Cucumber report for that revision
      When portable self-assurance evaluates the checkout with that report
      Then the report identifies scope "gherkin_executability"
      And it records the tested commit and execution report digest
      And parsed feature hashes match the imported report provenance
      And it makes no requirement-to-production-code verification claim

  Rule: Findings, unknown evidence, and tool failures remain distinct

    @SCN-3404
    Scenario: Recorded execution failure is an assurance finding
      Given a valid deterministic Cucumber report records a failed scenario
      And its provenance matches the evaluated repository revision
      When portable assurance ingests and evaluates that report
      Then the assurance command exits 0
      And tool_outcome is "completed"
      And an execution_failed finding identifies the failing execution
      And the report does not claim that a requirement is verified or failed

      Given the assurance command encounters "<failure>"
      When the command evaluates the selected revision
      Then it exits 2
      And its diagnostic report identifies the selected revision when resolution succeeded
      And the report is marked incomplete
      And the failure is not converted into an assurance finding

      Examples:
        | failure                               |
        | an unknown repository revision        |
        | malformed execution-report provenance |
        | an unreadable required ingestion input |
        | an unwritable report destination      |

    @SCN-3406
    Scenario: Workflow publication leaves repository branches unchanged
      Given a completed deterministic assurance report contains findings
      When the workflow publishes its artifact and job summary
      Then the artifact contains the report and its input manifest
      And the summary identifies the evaluated revision and finding count
      And no commit, branch update, pull-request comment, or deployment is requested
      And tracked repository content is unchanged

# Canonical acceptance specification for CI-02 (#37), M4 — REFINEMENT DRAFT / GATED.
# Implementation follows CI-01 and the M3 gate. Portable-locator comparison requires an owner
# disposition on comparison identity. See docs/adr/0012-closeout-scope-decisions.md.
@CI-02 @issue-37 @M4 @refinement-draft
Feature: CI-02: Comparable finding sets are classified by stable identity
  Finding identity is the existing stable fingerprint. Comparison requires complete, comparable,
  revision-bound reports; absence does not imply remediation.

  Rule: Identity determines new, unchanged, and resolved categories

    @SCN-3501
    Scenario: Compare the hand-labeled banking baselines
      Given complete comparable assurance reports for banking-demo baseline-a and baseline-b
      When the findings diff command compares baseline-a to baseline-b
      Then it reports 2 new findings
      And it reports 4 unchanged findings
      And it reports 0 resolved findings
      And the new finding types are reverification_required and verification_failed
      And the report includes both resolved revisions and both report digests

    @SCN-3502
    Scenario: Reverse comparison exposes the resolved category
      Given complete comparable assurance reports for banking-demo baseline-a and baseline-b
      When the findings diff command compares baseline-b to baseline-a
      Then it reports 0 new findings
      And it reports 4 unchanged findings
      And it reports 2 resolved findings
      And resolved means absent from the current comparable finding set
      And no verification evidence or requirement verdict is created

    @SCN-3503
    Scenario: Comparing a baseline with itself changes nothing
      Given a complete assurance report for banking-demo baseline-a
      When that report is compared with itself
      Then it reports 0 new findings
      And it reports 4 unchanged findings
      And it reports 0 resolved findings

    @SCN-3504
    Scenario: Payload changes do not replace an unchanged finding identity
      Given two comparable finding reports contain the same rule, finding type, and artifact IDs
      And those findings have different explanations and evidence references
      When the reports are compared
      Then the finding is classified as unchanged
      And its before and after payloads are both retained
      And neither payload is rewritten

  Rule: Unknown or incompatible inputs cannot imply resolution

    @SCN-3505
    Scenario Outline: Refuse an invalid comparison
      Given two report inputs differ by "<condition>"
      When the findings diff command compares them
      Then it exits 2 with code "findings-not-comparable"
      And it identifies the invalid input and reason
      And it returns no new, unchanged, or resolved classification

      Examples:
        | condition                                |
        | the previous resolved revision is absent |
        | the current resolved revision is absent  |
        | the current evaluation is incomplete     |
        | repository identities differ             |
        | evaluated rule scopes differ             |
        | policy versions differ                   |
        | a finding baseline contradicts its report|

    @SCN-3506
    Scenario: Source locators alone do not establish cross-revision continuity
      Given two portable finding reports use source-locator identities
      And no reviewed continuity mapping accompanies them
      When the findings diff command compares those reports
      Then it exits 2 with code "findings-not-comparable"
      And it reports that stable cross-revision identity is unavailable
      And it does not classify displaced findings as resolved and new

# Canonical acceptance specification for DT-01 (#20), M1.
# Source criteria: the GitHub story intake at
# https://github.com/anthonygraca/gherkin-knowledge-graph/issues/20 (verified 2026-11-13T00:52:26Z)
# and roadmap §6 F-02. Failure and boundary scenarios were added during refinement; the two
# intake scenarios keep their original wording.
# Verified by the pytest selectors mapped in DT-01.md and executed by the Cucumber suite (bdd/)
# from M2 onward.
@DT-01 @issue-20 @M1
Feature: DT-01: Requirements and Gherkin scenarios parsed into stable artifacts
  A requirement document declares its identity in YAML front matter. A Gherkin scenario
  declares its identity with an @SCN-nnn tag. Ingestion reads the repository at a pinned
  revision, never the working tree, and rejects malformed declarations instead of skipping
  them silently.

  @SCN-501
  Scenario: Requirement document parsed into an artifact
    Given the fixture repository checked out at "baseline-a"
    When the requirements are ingested
    Then an artifact "REQ-001" of type "requirement" exists with title "Instant withdrawal availability"
    And its locator is "requirements/REQ-001.md"
    And its content_hash is the sha256 of the file bytes at that revision
    And its metadata records status "active"

  @SCN-502
  Scenario: Scenario identity comes from the Gherkin tag
    Given "features/withdrawals.feature" contains the tag "@SCN-001"
    When the scenarios are ingested
    Then an artifact "SCN-001" of type "scenario" exists with locator "features/withdrawals.feature#SCN-001"
    And its title is the scenario name from the feature file
    And unannotated files produce no artifacts

  @SCN-503
  Scenario: A requirement without front matter is rejected
    Given a repository revision where "requirements/BROKEN.md" has no front matter block
    When the revision is ingested
    Then ingestion fails with an error naming "requirements/BROKEN.md"
    And no partial artifact set is returned

  @SCN-504
  Scenario: An untagged scenario creates no artifact
    Given a feature file containing a scenario without an "@SCN-nnn" tag
    When the scenarios are ingested
    Then no artifact is created for that scenario

  @SCN-505
  Scenario: A dangling scenario tag is rejected
    Given a feature file where "@SCN-999" is not followed by a "Scenario:" line
    When the scenarios are ingested
    Then ingestion fails with an error naming "@SCN-999"

  @SCN-506
  Scenario: Duplicate artifact identities are rejected
    Given two requirement documents declare the same id "REQ-900"
    When the revision is ingested
    Then ingestion fails with an error naming "REQ-900"

  @SCN-507
  Scenario: A symbolic revision is resolved once for the whole scan
    Given the fixture repository has tag "baseline-a" at a full commit SHA
    When the revision is ingested by tag name
    Then every artifact revision is that full commit SHA
    And ingesting the same revision by its SHA returns identical artifacts

  @SCN-508
  Scenario: Scenario-like text inside a doc string is data
    Given a tagged scenario whose step contains a doc string with "@SCN-999" and "Scenario: not real"
    When the scenarios are ingested
    Then only the real tagged scenario becomes an artifact
    And an opening delimiter line never also closes the same doc string
    And an unterminated doc string is an error

  @SCN-509
  Scenario: A malformed scenario identity token is rejected
    Given a scenario tagged "@SCN-99"
    When the scenarios are ingested
    Then ingestion fails with an error naming "@SCN-99"

  @SCN-510
  Scenario: Quoted front matter values keep their meaning
    Given a requirement whose id and status are quoted YAML strings with a trailing comment
    When the requirement is ingested
    Then the id is "REQ-900" without quotation marks
    And the status is "superseded" without the comment
    And a quoted title is stored without quotation marks

  @SCN-511
  Scenario: Invalid YAML front matter is rejected
    Given a requirement whose front matter has an unterminated quoted title
    When the revision is ingested
    Then ingestion fails with an error naming the file and the YAML problem

  As a project contributor, I want requirements, story acceptance criteria, implementation
  and verification evidence connected through a documented lifecycle, so that each change
  has a reviewable engineering basis.

  Rule: Each refined story keeps one authoritative acceptance specification

    Scenario: A refined story points to its canonical criteria
      Given the refined stories "FT-01" and "FT-02" have canonical criteria files under "docs/stories/"
      When a contributor needs the current acceptance criteria of "FT-01" or "FT-02"
      Then "docs/stories/FT-01.feature" and "docs/stories/FT-02.feature" carry the normative scenario wording
      And the M0 index cites each criterion as a link to its canonical scenario rather than restating the steps
      And the user-story issue form asks for the canonical acceptance specification before implementation

    @SCN-402
    Scenario: Migrated criteria keep their wording and their labels
      Given the M0 acceptance criteria recorded in "docs/stories/M0-foundation.md" at revision "efa824b5"
      When each migrated scenario in "FT-01.feature" and "FT-02.feature" is compared with that record
      Then every scenario title and step matches its source after leading indentation is removed
      And each scenario retains its original "AC-1.x" or "AC-2.x" label as a tag
      And the migrated scenarios number eight for "FT-01" and five for "FT-02"

  Rule: Every canonical scenario names how it will be verified

    @SCN-403
    Scenario: Each M0 scenario maps to a check that exists
      Given the canonical M0 scenarios "SCN-101" through "SCN-108" and "SCN-201" through "SCN-205"
      When the M0 acceptance verification map is inspected
      Then every scenario appears in exactly one mapping row
      And every pytest selector in the map resolves to a test function that exists under "backend/tests/"
      And the map states that a mapping row is not an executed result or an approval

    @SCN-404
    Scenario: A missing or unresolvable mapping is reported
      Given a copy of the M0 verification map with one scenario row removed and one selector renamed to a nonexistent test
      When the documented mapping-resolution procedure is applied to that copy
      Then it reports the unmapped scenario and the unresolvable selector
      And no scenario affected by those defects is reported as mapped

  Rule: Specification, execution and approval stay separate records

    @SCN-405
    Scenario: Status records claim neither execution nor approval
      Given "FT-01.feature", "FT-02.feature" and "FT-03.feature" have no Gherkin runner bindings
      When the migrated criteria are described in "STATUS.md", the M0 index, the issue map and the migration review record
      Then each record describes their verification as the mapped pytest checks
      And none claims that the scenarios were executed as Gherkin
      And none records an independent approval of the migration

  Rule: Scenario identity stays unique and traceable

    @SCN-406
    Scenario: Scenario and file identities are unique and traceable
      Given the canonical feature files under "docs/stories/"
      When their tags are collected
      Then every "@SCN-nnn" identifier is unique across those files
      And every canonical scenario carries exactly one "@SCN-nnn" tag
      And every canonical feature file names its story ID and its GitHub issue tag

# Canonical acceptance specification for PG-01 (#63), M2.
# Source criteria: the expanded-M2 intake recorded in issue #63 and session prompt §8A/§21.
# The fixture repositories under fixtures/external-*/ are ordinary projects that never adopted
# CTA conventions; their expected inventories are hand-counted.
@PG-01 @issue-63 @M2
Feature: PG-01: Portable read-only Gherkin ingestion and repository-scoped queries
  CTA indexes an existing Git repository at a pinned commit without modifying it or executing its
  code. Missing requirement metadata and missing runtime matching metadata are reported as absent,
  never as defects.

  Rule: Indexing is read-only and annotation-free

    @SCN-2201
    Scenario: Untagged scenarios are queryable without requirements metadata
      Given an independent Git repository contains valid untagged Gherkin scenarios
      And it has no CTA-specific source annotations or requirements inventory
      When CTA indexes a pinned commit in read-only mode
      Then the scenarios and their steps are available through repository-scoped queries
      And their exact source locations and revision are returned
      And the repository's tracked files remain byte-identical
      And missing requirement links are not reported as an implementation failure

    @SCN-2206
    Scenario: Indexing executes nothing from the repository
      Given an independent repository whose test hooks would write a sentinel file
      When CTA indexes it
      Then no hook or step definition from it was executed
      And the index reports zero modified files

  Rule: Missing metadata is unknown, not defective

    @SCN-2202
    Scenario: Step-definition resolution is unknown without framework evidence
      Given an external repository contains Gherkin steps
      And no supported framework matching report is available
      When CTA queries step-to-definition resolution
      Then the result is UNKNOWN or NOT_AVAILABLE
      And no undefined-step defect is asserted from missing metadata alone

  Rule: Supplied framework evidence is attributed

    @SCN-2203
    Scenario: Existing runtime metadata establishes executable relationships
      Given an external repository has a trusted Cucumber execution report
      When CTA ingests the report against the corresponding Git revision
      Then reported Gherkin step matches and outcomes are linked to their definitions
      And each relationship identifies its report provenance and tested commit
      And no unobserved production-code execution is inferred

  Rule: Imported runs keep their provenance

    @SCN-2207
    Scenario: A report without provenance cannot be attributed
      Given an external repository indexed at a pinned commit
      And a Cucumber report whose provenance sidecar is missing
      When CTA imports the report
      Then the import is refused with "report-not-applicable"
      And no execution records are stored

  Rule: Identity is repository-scoped

    @SCN-2204
    Scenario: Same scenario identifiers never collide across repositories
      Given two independent repositories use the same scenario tag and relative path
      When CTA indexes each at its own pinned revision
      Then each scenario has a distinct repository-scoped identity
      And querying one repository does not include the other's records

  Rule: The official Gherkin AST is preserved

    @SCN-2205
    Scenario: Rules, outlines, data tables, and doc strings are preserved
      Given an external repository contains a Rule and a Scenario Outline with Examples
      When its features are parsed at a pinned commit
      Then the rule and both example instances are queryable
      And the data table and doc string are kept as step arguments

# Follow-up acceptance slice for SETUP-01 (#8): commit-reference enforcement.
# Verified by pytest selectors in SETUP-01.md and executed by the Cucumber suite (bdd/) from M2
# onward; the pytest checks remain independent regression evidence.
@SETUP-01 @issue-8 @M0
# Executable-status note: Commit-history lint behaviour is verified by the 28 mapped pytest checks in backend/tests/test_commitlint.py; Cucumber bindings are pending under GT-02.
Feature: SETUP-01: Enforce traceability for new commits
  As a contributor, I want every new commit to name a registered work item
  so reviewers can trace repository changes to their intended purpose.

  Rule: New commit subjects identify their primary story or task

    @SCN-301
    Scenario: A contributor uses the new subject format
      Given issue 8 is registered as a story in the issue map
      When a commit message is "ci(traceability): [issue #8] enforce commit references"
      Then commit lint succeeds
      And the same message without the optional scope also succeeds

    @SCN-302
    Scenario: A body-only reference cannot replace the subject reference
      Given a commit subject is "ci: enforce commit references"
      And its body contains "Refs #8"
      When commit lint checks the message
      Then it fails and describes the required subject format

    @SCN-303
    Scenario: A reference must identify a registered story or task
      Given issue 999 is absent from the story and task tables
      When issue 999 appears in the required subject reference or a body reference line
      Then commit lint fails
      And feature rows and duplicate numbers mentioned only in prose are not valid work items

  Rule: Adoption preserves historical commits and checks every new contribution

    @SCN-304
    Scenario: A correct final commit does not hide an earlier invalid commit
      Given a legacy commit without an issue reference is the fixed adoption baseline
      And an invalid new commit follows it
      And a valid new commit follows the invalid commit
      When commit lint checks the new history
      Then it reports the invalid new commit
      And it does not report the legacy commit

    @SCN-305
    Scenario: Pull request history is selected from the actual branch
      Given a topic branch and its target both contain the adoption baseline
      And both branches contain independent later commits
      When commit lint checks the topic head excluding the target history
      Then it checks every topic commit absent from the target
      And it excludes commits already reachable from the target

    @SCN-306
    Scenario: Real merge commits and their side branches retain traceability
      Given a new merge commit integrates a topic branch
      When either the merge message or a topic commit lacks the required issue reference
      Then commit lint fails
      And a conforming merge with conforming topic commits succeeds

  Rule: Validation uses attributable local inputs and fails on missing history

    @SCN-307
    Scenario: A later map edit cannot repair an invalid historical reference
      Given a new commit references an issue absent from its own issue map
      And the working tree later adds that issue
      When commit lint checks the commit
      Then it fails using the map at that commit

    @SCN-308
    Scenario: Missing Git history is not a passing check
      Given a selected revision is unavailable or the repository is shallow
      When commit lint checks the history
      Then it fails with an operational error
      And it does not claim the selected commits passed
